interpretation: The placement of expectation changes the controlled object: pNB controls the expected squared Hilbert-space norm of the random residual, whereas gNB controls only the squared norm of its expectation. Jensen therefore gives pNB implies gNB, while averaging in gNB can discard sample-to-sample variation, so no reverse implication follows here. The later routes to RH are conditional rather than intrinsic to these definitions: the roadmap pairs pNB with Assumption (P), and pairs the stated gNB converse with a moment assumption and coefficient-growth condition (C).

nonparaphrase_operation: Comparing the two representations isolates the information lost by averaging before measuring error: gNB can retain a small mean residual even when individual residuals vary, while pNB also penalizes that variation. This explains the Jensen direction without treating either later set of sufficient hypotheses as part of the criteria themselves.

interpretation: The proof converts a random approximation into a deterministic Nyman-Beurling witness by satisfying two constraints at one outcome. pNB and Markov yield a strict lower bound P(A_n)>1-nu for the small-error event, while Assumption (P) gives P(B_n)>nu for simultaneous admissibility 0<Z_{k,n}<=1. Their strict probability sum exceeds one, forcing P(A_n intersect B_n)>0; evaluating at an outcome in that intersection supplies both the approximation and admissible deterministic parameters. This theorem and this extraction argument do not cover pNB without (P), but they do not prove that every possible pNB-to-RH argument requires (P).
